title: The strengthened quantum Hamming bound of Yu, Lai, and Oh
abstract: We prove a conjecture of Yu, Lai, and Oh: their rounded family of strengthened quantum Hamming bounds, which interpolates between Hamming-type bounds and the Singleton bound, holds for arbitrary exact quantum subspaces of dimension $K>1$. The result covers every integer local dimension $p\ge2$, every integer $t\ge1$, both distances $2t+1$ and $2t+2$, and every interpolation parameter $e\in\{0,\ldots,t\}$. Yu, Lai, and Oh proved these bounds for pure codes and for general codes of distance three or four; the case $e=0$ contains the ordinary quantum Hamming bound for general codes, recently proved by Zhang and Chen. More generally, for $p\ge3$, we prove the inequality $Kf(0)\le p^n\mathbb{E}f(X)$, where $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,1-p^{-2})$, for every real polynomial $f$ of degree at most $D$, with $2\le D<d$, that is nonnegative on $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and positive at zero; here $n$ and $d$ are the code length and distance.
comment: 106 pages; computational certificates and reproduction code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23535642

bite.hook: We prove a conjecture of Yu, Lai, and Oh for arbitrary exact quantum subspaces of dimension K>1.
tldr: Proved a conjecture by Yu, Lai, and Oh regarding a rounded family of strengthened quantum Hamming bounds.
Used mathematical proofs covering every integer local dimension, distance, and interpolation parameter.
Showed the bounds hold for arbitrary exact quantum subspaces of dimension greater than one.
bite.whyItMatters: Quantum error correction relies heavily on theoretical bounds to understand how much information can be safely stored. Confirming this major conjecture strengthens the mathematical foundation for designing better quantum codes.
bite.eli5: Imagine trying to pack as many secret messages as possible into a box without them getting mixed up. Mathematicians just proved a strict rulebook for how tightly you can pack quantum messages without errors ruining everything.
